Three orders on the same six requirements

• each order is named by its lowest requirement
  • on target lowest is the order of the sections before
  • fuel and control energy lie below every requirement
Upright for the last 2 s: every order gives the same landings
• with upright for the last 2 s, all six requirements can hold together
Upright for the last 2 s: every order gives the same landings

• with upright for the last 2 s, all six requirements can hold together
  • in every order, a landing that meets all six beats every landing that violates one
  • so the optimal landings trade fuel against control energy
Upright for the last 5 s: the requirements conflict

• no landing meets all six: at most five hold together
  • the order decides which requirements give way
  • on target lowest has several optimal landings, and the one shown breaks the tilt limit
The violated requirements depend on the order

• on target lowest violates on target with upright, with the tilt limit, or with both
  • upright lowest violates upright alone, soft touchdown lowest soft touchdown alone

Every order of the case study has the same optimal landings when the six requirements can hold together.
Trade-offs across requirements arise when they conflict.
Three landings that hold the tilt limit lie on one trade-off

• every point holds glide cone, tilt limit and speed limit
  • its height is the least upright violation within the bounds on the other two axes
  • each order picks a different point of the trade-off
